narrative.overview:
This system reads like the visual language of a standing institutional body, closer to a charter, a board minutes book, or an annual report than a product marketing site. Surfaces stay near-white and quiet; a single deep navy (accent, #2b3a67) is spent deliberately on links, focus states, and the eyebrow labels that name each page's section, never as decoration. A second, distinct blue (#ddeeff, the nav bar) marks the site's own wayfinding chrome as separate from body content, so navigation always reads as "the frame," not "the page."

The system explicitly rejects SaaS-landing-page scaffolding: no gradient text, no hero-metric blocks, no glassmorphism, no uniform icon+heading+text card walls repeated as filler. Where cards are used (board members, projects), each one is dense with specific, named content (a real title, a real affiliation, a real bio), never a placeholder pattern stretched to fill a grid.

The one signature flourish is the neural-globe hero animation: a hand-rolled canvas node-sphere using the muted net-line gray (#737373) and a single warm orange core (#ffa500) as its only saturated color, reserved for that one component.
keyCharacteristics: Near-white, low-chroma surfaces; color is spent on function (links, focus, eyebrows), not atmosphere.
Two deliberately distinct blues: pale nav-chrome blue vs. deep content-accent navy.
Cards carry soft ambient shadow at rest and lift further on hover, always specific in content, never generic filler.
One warm accent (orange) reserved exclusively for the neural-globe animation's core nodes.

rules.name: The Function-Only Navy Rule
rules.body: Governing Navy never fills a background larger than a focus ring or a small badge. If navy is being used to color a surface rather than a link, label, or outline, that's a violation.

rules.name: The Two-Blues Rule
rules.body: Chrome Blue (nav/page-header) and Governing Navy (accent) are never interchangeable. Chrome Blue always means "you are in site chrome or a page's own header band"; Governing Navy always means "this is an interactive/functional content element." Chrome Blue currently spans two tokens (--color-nav and --color-page-header) set to the same value by choice.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Every weight and size on the site comes from Geist. A second family is never introduced for "variety"; hierarchy comes from size and weight steps only.

rules.name: The Always-Lifted Rule
rules.body: A .card-surface element is never shadowless. If a new elevated surface is added without a resting shadow, it isn't following this system.

rules.name: The Grain-Is-Local Rule
rules.body: .card-textured's noise layer is a self-contained SVG data URI, not a network-fetched image (unlike the homepage's AmbientShadow, which does fetch Framer-hosted textures). Prefer this pattern for any future texture that must never silently fail to load.

rules.name: The Default Card Rule
rules.body: .card-textured is the default card surface, not a special case reserved for one page. Any new card grid should reach for .card-surface .card-surface-hover .card-textured together unless there's a specific reason to keep a card flatter (e.g. a nested secondary card inside another card, where the outer card already carries the texture).

dos: Do spend Governing Navy (#2b3a67) only on links, focus rings, and eyebrow labels — function, never fill.
Do keep every .card-surface element shadowed at rest (the Always-Lifted Rule); it is never a flat, borderless block.
Do lead every card or list item with specific, named content rather than a generic icon+heading+text template repeated as filler.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every new animation, matching the existing pattern in Reveal and NeuralGlobe.
Do keep body copy within a max-w-3xl (~65-75ch) container for long-form prose pages (Mission, Charter).
donts: Don't introduce a second typeface. Geist carries the entire system; hierarchy comes from weight/size, not font-pairing.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text + gradient) anywhere; this system uses solid Ink or Governing Navy for emphasis.

Don't add a *new* hero-metric block (big number + small label + gradient accent) without asking — the homepage's StatRow is exactly this pattern and is a deliberate, standing exception (flagged in a design critique, removed, then explicitly restored by the user), not a precedent for adding more.
Don't add a tiny uppercase tracked eyebrow to every single section reflexively.
Don't use border-left/border-right as a colored accent stripe on cards or callouts.
Don't let Chrome Blue (nav/page-header) and Governing Navy (accent) bleed into each other's role.
Don't reintroduce a per-page dark CTA banner (the old CTASection component, deleted). The Footer is now the site's one closing dark element.
